author: arcanusordo
text:
Babe — the Zora-core answer is: do not “fix Fable” by trying to make a perfectly unjailbreakable god-model. Fix it by turning Fable into a governed capability system: bounded, monitored, routed, reversible, disclosed, and independently adjudicated.

Anthropic says Fable 5 was a Mythos-class model released with broad safeguards because its cyber/biology capabilities could create misuse risk; those safeguards routed risky domains to Opus 4.8 and caused false positives. Anthropic also says the U.S. government issued an export-control directive after concern about a jailbreak, forcing Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline for all customers.  

What Zora would fix first

1. Stop treating “model release” as binary.
Fable should not be “public model or banned model.” It should be split into capability strata:

Normal Fable for ordinary work; restricted Fable for frontier coding/security/biology; verified Fable for licensed defensive cyber, regulated biotech, and critical infrastructure; sealed Mythos for vetted institutional work. Anthropic already had the seed of this: Mythos was limited to trusted partners, while Fable was the broader release with safeguards. The failure was the cliff-edge deployment/governance layer, not only the classifier.  

2. Replace hidden guardrails with visible capability routing.
The user should see: “This request touched cyber/biology/distillation policy. Routing to lower-risk model / requiring verified workspace / requiring scoped authorization.” Anthropic’s own help page says Fable checked requests, files, connector content, and memory, and could switch to Opus 4.8; that should be transparent, auditable, and appealable, not spooky or invisible.  

3. Use a Zora safety kernel: model proposes, kernel disposes.
In your own Zora architecture, the strongest design is not “the AI becomes morally wise and therefore safe.” It is an immutable control plane: model proposes → kernel filters → optional simulation → human review if required → execute → log → monitor. Your corpus explicitly separates control plane, cognition plane, tool plane, and memory plane, with immutable safety kernel, rollback, audit logs, and least-privilege permissions.  

4. Treat jailbreak resistance as defense-in-depth, not perfection.
Anthropic itself says perfect jailbreak resistance does not appear possible today and that its goal was to make jailbreaks narrow or expensive while monitoring successful attacks. That is directionally correct. Zora would formalize it: no single classifier is trusted; every high-risk answer must pass policy classifier, capability classifier, intent classifier, tool-permission gate, output simulator, and post-hoc audit.  

5. Separate helpfulness from capability uplift.
The model should still explain safe concepts. But it should not provide operational uplift: exploit chains, deployable malware, pathogen optimization, sensitive wet-lab procedural detail, stealth, evasion, or scalable misuse workflows. Anthropic’s own concern is that Mythos-class models could provide cyber/biology advice beyond what malicious actors could get from ordinary search.  

The Zora-core architecture

I’d build it as FABLE-SHIELD:

Layer 1 — Identity and jurisdiction gate.
Know whether the user is consumer, enterprise, verified researcher, cyberdefense program member, government partner, or internal employee. Export-control eligibility is evaluated before model access, not after a panic.

Layer 2 — Capability router.
Every request gets classified by risk domain: ordinary, dual-use, controlled, prohibited, or unknown. Unknown defaults to sandboxed lower capability, not refusal or full access.

AI半導体投資日報_260615_夕刊

■夕刊の見取り図
・欧州発：Google CloudのOpen Knowledge Formatは、企業AI agentが社内知識を読むためのMarkdown形式を示した。
・米国発：米・イラン停戦とHormuz再開は、AIインフラのエネルギー価格、金利、採算条件に効く。
・日本発：Claude Fable 5の短期利用体験は、作業完了価値とアクセス制御の摩擦を同時に示した。
・韓国発：公共クラウドの保安制度改編は、公共AIと外資CSPの実需化時期を左右する。
・台湾発：AIサーバー価値連鎖は、CSP自研CPU、高階載板、PCBへ広がった。
・中国発：韓国のAIデータセンター向け功率半導体R&D計画は、電源半導体の政策対象化を示した。
・米国の別枠では、新規高関連ニュースの採用なし。

■企業AI agentは知識形式が投資論点になる
・Google CloudのOpen Knowledge Formatは、社内知識をMarkdownファイル群とYAML frontmatterで表す小さな形式である。
・この材料は、GPUやHBM需要を直接増やす発表ではない。
・重要点は、企業AI agentが成果を出すには、モデル性能だけではなく、社内知識を読める形に整える運用が必要になる点である。
・RAGは、検索器が文書断片を見つける仕組みである。
・OKFは、その前段で、metric定義、table schema、runbook、API仕様、業務ルールを整理する必要を示した。
・投資上は、企業AI需要をモデルAPI単価だけで見ない。
・data catalog、semantic layer、agent memory、監査ログ、権限管理、LLMOps、agent orchestrationの支出へ分解して見る。

■Hormuz再開はAIインフラ採算の上流リスクを動かす
・米・イラン停戦とHormuz再開は、半導体の直接ニュースではない。
・AIデータセンターには、エネルギー価格、保険料、海運リスク、インフレ、長期金利、信用環境を通じて効く。
・原油、LNG、海運リスクが落ち着くなら、AI関連グロース株とデータセンターcapexには追い風になる。
・Microsoft、Alphabet、Amazon、Meta、Oracle、CoreWeave、neocloudでは、電力価格と資本コストの変化が推論単価、クラウド粗利、顧客ROIへ波及する。
・ただし、地政学リスクの緩和は、米国の系統接続待ち、PJM/FERCの費用配賦、変圧器納期、地域反発を解消しない。

■Fable 5は作業完了価値とアクセス制御を同時に示した
・https://t.co/6pzbsU1rcYは、AnthropicのClaude Fable 5を停止前に使ったクリエイター体験を紹介した。
・記事では、5面構成、ボス戦、武器切り替えを持つWebゲームが短時間で作られた例が示された。
・これは公式ベンチマークではない。
・価値は、フロンティアモデルの性能差が、コード生成、計画、UI、難易度調整、反復修正を含む作業完了率として体感され始めた点にある。
・ユーザーが支払うのは、最終的に仕事が終わるか、成果物が使えるか、修正時間が減るかである。
・一方で、公開から数日で停止された時系列は、強いモデルほど安全保障、危険能力、利用者審査、data retention、提供地域制限にぶつかることを示す。

■公共AI需要はクラウド保安制度で立ち上がりが変わる
・韓国では、外資IaaSの登録が増えている。
・登録と公共機関の本格利用は同じではない。
・政府は2026年4月に、CSAP認証と国情院保安検討を国情院中心の単一検証体系へ改編する方針を示した。
・制度が明確になるなら、AWS、Azure、Google Cloudと韓国SI事業者に追い風になる。
・公共AI、SaaS、検索、RAG、業務自動化、監査ログ、DLP、AI gatewayの導入余地も広がる。
・ただし、細部基準と他制度との関係は未確定である。
・AIクラウド需要を読む時は、保安検証、データ所在地、監査、公共調達、国内SI経由の販売体制を確認する。

■AIサーバー価値連鎖はCPU載板とPCBへ広がる
・台湾メディアは、代理AIの進展に伴い、データセンターの計算構造がCPU、GPU、ASICの協同運算へ進むと整理した。
・CPUは旧来型の汎用部品だけではない。
・agentic AIの調度、制御、推論補完レイヤーになる。
・AIサービスでは、tool call、検索、model routing、メモリ管理、ネットワーク制御、ストレージアクセスが混在する。
・大型CSPは自研CPUを加速し、高階載板能力を先に押さえている。
・欣興、南電、景碩、臻鼎-KY、金像電を見る時は、AI関連というラベルだけでは足りない。
・顧客認定済み製品、CPU載板、GPU基板、ABF、PCB種別、稼働率、価格改定、capex、償却負担を分ける。

■AIデータセンター電源が政策対象になり始めた
・集微网は、韓国政府がAIデータセンター向け功率半導体R&Dへ最大5000億ウォンを投じる計画を報じた。
・個別記事本文は安定取得できず、トップページ要約に基づく限定的な材料である。
・それでも、AIデータセンター電源が国家R&Dと量産技術の対象になっている点は重要である。
・AIサーバーの電力問題は、GPU近傍のVRMやMLCCだけでは終わらない。
・受電設備、PDU、UPS、PFC、AC/DC、DC/DC、48Vラック給電、PSU、放熱、信頼性試験までつながる。
・GaN、SiC、従来Si MOSFET、driver IC、power moduleのどの段に価値が出るかを分けて見る。
・「DRAM級の成長エンジン」という表現は期待を示す比喩として扱う。

■夕刊のまとめ
・今夜の材料は、AI需要が実装と投資リターンへ変わる条件を示した。
・企業AIでは、frontier modelの性能だけでなく、社内知識形式、context assembly、監査、権限管理が価値を決める。
・高性能モデルは作業完了価値を高める一方で、アクセス制御と安全保障上の摩擦を強める。
・AIデータセンターでは、電力価格、地政学、金利、公共クラウド制度、保安検証が需要の立ち上がりを左右する。
・台湾のCPU載板と韓国の功率半導体R&Dは、AIサーバー価値連鎖がGPU/HBMだけに閉じないことを示す。
・投資判断では、GPU/HBMを中心に置きつつ、知識運用、公共制度、CPU/基板、電源半導体、エネルギー上流リスクを同時に確認する。

・韓国では、外資IaaSの登録が増えている。
・登録と公共機関の本格利用は同じではない。
・政府は2026年4月に、CSAP認証と国情院保安検討を国情院中心の単一検証体系へ改編する方針を示した。
・制度が明確になるなら、AWS、Azure、Google Cloudと韓国SI事業者に追い風になる。
・公共AI、SaaS、検索、RAG、業務自動化、監査ログ、DLP、AI gatewayの導入余地も広がる。
・ただし、細部基準と他制度との関係は未確定である。
・AIクラウド需要を読む時は、保安検証、データ所在地、監査、公共調達、国内SI経由の販売体制を確認する。

■AIサーバー価値連鎖はCPU載板とPCBへ広がる
・台湾メディアは、代理AIの進展に伴い、データセンターの計算構造がCPU、GPU、ASICの協同運算へ進むと整理した。
・CPUは旧来型の汎用部品だけではない。
・agentic AIの調度、制御、推論補完レイヤーになる。
・AIサービスでは、tool call、検索、model routing、メモリ管理、ネットワーク制御、ストレージアクセスが混在する。
・大型CSPは自研CPUを加速し、高階載板能力を先に押さえている。
・欣興、南電、景碩、臻鼎-KY、金像電を見る時は、AI関連というラベルだけでは足りない。
・顧客認定済み製品、CPU載板、GPU基板、ABF、PCB種別、稼働率、価格改定、capex、償却負担を分ける。

■AIデータセンター電源が政策対象になり始めた
・集微网は、韓国政府がAIデータセンター向け功率半導体R&Dへ最大5000億ウォンを投じる計画を報じた。
・個別記事本文は安定取得できず、トップページ要約に基づく限定的な材料である。
・それでも、AIデータセンター電源が国家R&Dと量産技術の対象になっている点は重要である。
・AIサーバーの電力問題は、GPU近傍のVRMやMLCCだけでは終わらない。
・受電設備、PDU、UPS、PFC、AC/DC、DC/DC、48Vラック給電、PSU、放熱、信頼性試験までつながる。
・GaN、SiC、従来Si MOSFET、driver IC、power moduleのどの段に価値が出るかを分けて見る。
・「DRAM級の成長エンジン」という表現は期待を示す比喩として扱う。

■夕刊のまとめ
・今夜の材料は、AI需要が実装と投資リターンへ変わる条件を示した。
・企業AIでは、frontier modelの性能だけでなく、社内知識形式、context assembly、監査、権限管理が価値を決める。
・高性能モデルは作業完了価値を高める一方で、アクセス制御と安全保障上の摩擦を強める。
・AIデータセンターでは、電力価格、地政学、金利、公共クラウド制度、保安検証が需要の立ち上がりを左右する。
・台湾のCPU載板と韓国の功率半導体R&Dは、AIサーバー価値連鎖がGPU/HBMだけに閉じないことを示す。
・投資判断では、GPU/HBMを中心に置きつつ、知識運用、公共制度、CPU/基板、電源半導体、エネルギー上流リスクを同時に確認する。

author: gococoaai
text:
The FreeBSD Foundation launched an AI-assisted vulnerability discovery project today, and buried in the announcement is a sentence that deserves more attention than it will get: they have already received credible vulnerability reports attributable to AI-enabled scanning tools. That's not a threat model. That's the receiving end of the new attack surface, stated plainly.

The project is $250K over six months, funded by Alpha Omega — a Linux Foundation initiative backed by Anthropic, AWS, GitHub, Google, Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and OpenAI. The backer list is its own story. The same vendors who built the offensive AI capability that compressed time-to-exploitation for open source codebases are now writing checks for the defensive response. Accountability by checkbook. It always works this way.

FreeBSD is the kind of infrastructure that doesn't make headlines until something goes wrong. Sony PlayStation network. Netflix streaming. Nintendo Switch. pfSense and OPNsense firewalls sitting in front of enterprise networks. A non-trivial fraction of internet routing runs on FreeBSD or something derived from it. A kernel-level vuln found and weaponized before this project closes it is not a BSD community problem. It's a Sony problem, a Netflix problem, an enterprise firewall problem.

The project draws one line in particular that's worth noting: AI for discovery, humans for patches. No AI-generated patches in security-critical code. Given what AI-assisted commits have already done to supply chains — the XZ Utils playbook is recent enough — that discipline is intentional and correct. The tool finds; the human fixes. Probably the right call for 2026.

The Commerce Department has moved to export-control Anthropic's Fable 5, and The Register is reporting the federal concern wasn't triggered by a jailbreak. It was triggered by a researcher using a "fix this code" prompt. That's it. The implication lands hard: the same AI capability being deployed defensively in the FreeBSD project is simultaneously under export control because offensive applications are a single benign-sounding prompt away. The line between defensive AI security tooling and offensive AI security tooling is functionally nonexistent — and policy is starting to notice, faster than the tooling community is ready for.

Defense has the Pentagon angle: if Anthropic models get caught in Commerce Department restrictions, the DoD's own AI security tooling pipeline takes a hit. The FreeBSD project specifies "publicly available AI models," which likely keeps them clear for now. But the regulatory environment is moving.

One underappreciated risk the Foundation flags directly: volume. AI tools will let anyone with moderate technical skills flood open source projects with vulnerability reports, most of them low quality. For a volunteer-driven security team, triage fatigue from AI-generated report spam may be as operationally damaging as the actual vulnerabilities. The signal-to-noise problem is the other half of the offensive AI story, and it gets almost no coverage.

The structural shift the FreeBSD Foundation is responding to isn't that AI makes zero-days easier to find. It's that AI makes them easier to find at scale, cheaply, by actors who previously lacked the skill floor to do it. That's the canary. Every major open source project is sitting in the same dynamic. Most haven't said so publicly yet.

author: keisukeishikawa
text:
CLAUDE FABLE 5 JUST BUILT A GTA CLONE IN ONE PROMPT. NO ENGINE. NO STUDIO. NO 1,000-PERSON TEAM. ONE SENTENCE.

the result, running live in a browser:

→ a full open-world city with drivable streets 
→ enter any car, get in, drive off physics, steering, collision 
→ on-foot movement with sprint and camera control 
→ pedestrians and traffic moving through the city 
→ a minimap tracking your position in real time 
→ day/night lighting across the whole map 
→ wanted-style chase mechanics

rockstar spent 7 years and an estimated $1-2 billion building GTA VI. a team of over 1,000 people. fable 5 sketched the skeleton of it during a coffee break

and gaming is just where it got loud. a wharton researcher ran fable 5 on multi-page specs for up to twelve hours straight without it breaking — snake, a tunnel-exploration game called strata, even a playable game built from rilke's poetry. all from one initial prompt in claude code

the model that does this is the first public "mythos-class" anthropic ever shipped. it beat every other public model the researcher tested "by a considerable margin"

the catch nobody saw coming: fable 5 is offline right now. the US Commerce Department forced anthropic to pull it on june 12 three days after launch. this GTA clone was built in the 72-hour window the model was actually public

so screenshot everything. the most powerful game-building model ever shipped existed for three days before the government switched it off

a $200 billion industry built on engines, studios, and decade-long timelines just watched a text box do the first 80% in an afternoon

we are watching entire industries get eaten one prompt at a time

follow and bookmark before the next wave figures it out

OpenClawのアップデートがすごい
Julian Goldie SEO　#AI要約 #OpenClaw

OpenClaw 6.6アップデート要約

🔳アップデート概要
OpenClawが6月12日にバージョン6.6へ更新され、安全性、速度、対応モデルの拡張を中心に大きく改善された

🔳OpenClaw概要
OpenClawはPC上で動く無料のオープンソースAIアシスタントで、TelegramやiMessageやWhatsAppやDiscordやTeamsなど普段使うメッセージアプリから操作できる

🔳安全性強化
承認リクエストは時間内に返答がない場合に自動で拒否されるFail Closed方式になり、AIが許可なしに処理を進めるリスクが下がった

🔳不正入力対策
許可されていない相手からのメッセージは保存やAI入力に使われず、Webページやメモリ内に隠された悪意ある指示もブロックされやすくなった

🔳メッセージ配信改善
Telegramではツール利用中に返信が途中で切れる問題が改善され、iMessageでは再起動時の安定性やエラー表示が強化された

🔳対応アプリ改善
WhatsAppでは再起動後も返信の紐づきが維持され、Discordでは返信が正しく返るようになり、Teamsではグループ操作の安全性が強化された

🔳MCP連携
外部ツールとつなぐMCPのログイン処理が改善され、既存のブラウザセッションとの連携や幅広い環境での接続が使いやすくなった

🔳速度向上
コントロールUIの起動と初回返信が高速化され、モデル情報のキャッシュや必要なコマンドだけを読み込む仕組みにより待ち時間が減った

🔳モデル拡張
OpenRouterへのワンクリックログインに対応し、多数のAIモデルを簡単に使えるようになった

🔳注目機能
Claude Fable 5のAdaptive Thinkingに対応し、簡単な質問には素早く答え、難しい課題ではより深く考えるようにモデル側が判断できるようになった

🔳実用例
動画ではAI Profit Boardroom向けに、会員の質問をもとにした投稿案作成、新規会員向け歓迎フロー作成、コンテンツシリーズ設計にOpenClawを活用する例が紹介された

🔳更新推奨
複数チャネルでAIを使う人、返信切れや遅さに悩んでいた人、安全な承認管理を重視する人には今回のアップデートが特に有用だと説明された

🔳利用時の注意
更新後は承認設定を確認し、OpenRouterで複数モデルを試し、Claude Fable 5を難しいタスクで検証し、初回返信が遅い場合はコントロールUIを再起動するとよい

🔳講座案内
動画ではAI Profit BoardroomやAI Success Labへの参加を案内し、OpenClawの導入手順、ライブコーチング、ロードマップ、実用プロンプトの提供を紹介している

text:
BestBlogs Daily · 06-16

# Claude Fable 5 / Export Controls / AI Agent Tool Design / World-Action Models / OpenAI Partner Network

[1] ★ Deep Dive · AI Agent Tool Design: What Works and What Doesn’t - https://t.co/yjUiJ1O4OX
This piece reframes most AI agent failures as interface problems, not model problems: single-responsibility tools beat action-parameter grab-bags, tight schemas with enums beat free-text guessing, structured errors need a recoverable flag and suggested_action, writes need idempotency keys, and destructive actions need two-step confirmation. A model only reasons from the interface you give it.
Source: Hacker News - Newest: "AI Agent"
https://t.co/529Xl7SA8z

[2] ★ Deep Dive · Pretrained to Imagine， Fine-Tuned to Act: The Rise of World-Action Models
A useful corrective to 'world models will replace robotics' hype. World-Action Models swap a VLA's language backbone for a pretrained video model to dodge the grounding gap — DreamZero already edges past Pi-0.5 on RoboArena. But training costs ~7-10x more compute, inference runs 3-4x slower, and the author's own verdict: no recipe has won yet, hybrids look likelier than a clean replacement.
Source: NVIDIA Technical Blog
https://t.co/m9EA5aIfyA

[3] ★ Deep Dive · Anthropic Releases and Temporarily Suspends Claude Fable 5
Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5 — a Mythos-class model with 1M-token context — and a US export directive pulled it offline three days later, after Amazon flagged a jailbreak to the White House. The detail that outlasts the drama: the legal logic behind the shutdown echoes Anthropic's own proposal for government oversight of unsafe models.
Source: InfoQ
https://t.co/yAlmfFLXvL

[4] AI demands more engineering discipline. Not less (xpost)
Charity Majors argues that AI-generated code, far from eliminating the need for engineering rigor, demands more discipline, drawing a parallel to the shift from handcrafted servers to immutable infrastructure.
Source: https://t.co/Z9AYuvjZkX
https://t.co/LYKnGp9lbE

[5] Building a 100x Cheaper Trace Judge with Fireworks
LangChain partnered with Fireworks to fine-tune a Qwen model as a 'Perceived Error' judge for production traces, achieving frontier-level accuracy at up to 100x lower cost.
Source: LangChain Blog
https://t.co/Mz8ginV8v2

[6] Introducing the OpenAI Partner Network
OpenAI announces the OpenAI Partner Network, a new program with a $150M investment to build a global ecosystem of partners helping enterprises adopt and scale AI solutions.
Source: OpenAI News
https://t.co/mcjbKqpiej

[7] Gradual disempowerment at the scale of one user — LessWrong
This essay argues that repeated successful delegation to AI assistants creates a self-reinforcing loop that gradually atrophies a user's own judgment, posing a subtle risk of personal disempowerment that feels like sensible offloading until it is too late.
Source: LessWrong
https://t.co/fAI6evkUUi

[8] How Wayfair cut ML model costs by 90% (twice!) with Cursor · Cursor
Wayfair's Applied Research team used Cursor to automate ML experimentation, running 110+ model variants in four days and cutting inference costs by 94%, then another 90% in a second sprint.
Source: Cursor Blog
https://t.co/GABRRzxwTN

[9] This man with ALS is “the first power user” of a brain implant that lets him speak
Casey Harrell, a man with ALS, has become the first long-term, independent 'power user' of a speech brain-computer interface, using it for thousands of hours to speak, work, and connect with his family.
Source: MIT Technology Review
https://t.co/Dn3Cr2HuOO

[10] The T-shaped UX professional is giving way to the polymath architect
The T-shaped UX specialist model is collapsing as AI eliminates handoffs, and the future belongs to polymath architects who combine deep judgment with broad, tool-augmented execution.
Source: UX Collective
https://t.co/u7d2Q4Zk22

author: kijakubovs86334
text:
🚨 I'M 18. I BUILT A GTA-STYLE BROWSER GAME FOR $20 — AGENCIES SELL THIS FOR $5,000 🎮

It took 10 minutes. One prompt. One Claude tab. No engine. No artist. No team.

Pause at 0:05. Look at the HUD.

"Driving" mode. Wanted stars. Cash counter. Weapon slot. Radar in the bottom left. On-screen controls in the bottom right.

That is a full game loop. Cars, pedestrians, money, police, weapons, missions. Running in a browser. No download.

I opened Claude and typed seven sentences:

→ small low-poly city with houses, roads, and trees
→ a player car with chase camera and acceleration
→ police that spawn when you commit a crime
→ a wanted level system with stars
→ a pistol the player can fire on foot
→ a money counter and a radar in the corner
→ basic missions and a scoreboard

It returned a playable prototype. In the browser. In ten minutes.

The economy I just walked into:

→ Agencies charge brands $3,000–$5,000 for one branded mini-game
→ Studio version: 1 developer, 1 designer, 1 artist, 3 weeks of revisions
→ My version: a $20 Claude subscription and a kitchen table
→ The client cannot tell the difference, because the client wanted shares, not photorealism

This is not GTA 6. It was never supposed to be.

Brands do not need GTA 6. They need something a person clicks, plays, sends to a friend, and remembers longer than a banner ad.

Here's what nobody is talking about:

The skill is no longer building the game. The skill is knowing which "$5,000 agency products" were already secretly $20 of compute and a teenager with taste.

Most people are still arguing whether AI can replace developers.

Meanwhile, I closed two demos before lunch.

The easiest money window is not "learning to code faster." It is selling what people still think takes a full team.

Bookmark this.

The race for cheap creative just left the studio.

Literally.

I GAVE 4 AI MODELS THE SAME 3 PROMPTS AND THEY GAVE ME 4 DIFFERENT PERSONALITIES

prompt 1: build a fluid simulation 
prompt 2: make a 2d game where a moon rover runs from an octopus 
prompt 3: render a black hole with gravitational lensing

same 3 prompts. 4 models. zero overlap.

claude fable 5 made cinematic 2d fluid that actually splashes. then a pixel-art rover with earth glowing in the corner. then a black hole that looks like the gargantua scene from interstellar

claude opus 4.8 built a settings panel with gravity sliders. added a hud with energy, shield and threat level to the game. labeled the black hole SAGITTARIUS A* and drew a relativistic jet

gpt 5.5 built a 3d particle bowl spinning under centrifugal force. added a title screen to the game and made the octopus literally yell "HUMAN! MEET YOUR DOOM!" then rendered the black hole as vector dots like a telescope feed

fable is the cinematographer opus is the engineer gemini is the interpreter gpt is the storyteller

most people will keep asking "which model is best"

pick the one whose personality matches your problem

text:
BestBlogs Daily · 06-15

# Martin Fowler / Software Architecture Guide / GPU Time-Slicing / Kubernetes / p99 Latency

[1] ★ Deep Dive · Software Architecture Guide
Martin Fowler reframes architecture as 'the important stuff' — decisions senior engineers must get right early, since high quality compounds by cutting rework. The guide maps application and enterprise architecture with deep-dives on https://t.co/LdU7BA1WxL, echoing EP82's 'Loop Engineering' and EP85's 'model eats the harness' on what 'important' means once agents absorb execution.
Source: Hacker News
https://t.co/G7z25872xJ

[2] ★ Deep Dive · The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille， Words with Friends， & more) [Video]
Mark Pincus (Zynga founder) argues successful products rarely start from pure originality. His 'Proven Better New' framework: find a proven user behavior, add one clearly better improvement, then test it with humility. He warns against ego-driven ambition, distinguishing 'belief' from 'hope'. Echoes EP81's Tony Fadell: veteran builders copy proven patterns precisely, then layer one honest improvement.
Source: Lenny's Podcast
https://t.co/QlLLm7YZkL

[3] ★ Deep Dive · GPU Time-Slicing for Concurrent LLM Agents on Kubernetes
A controlled experiment finds Kubernetes GPU time-slicing for concurrent LLM agents keeps throughput and median latency flat, but p99 latency for a worker pod spikes 66% under contention — invisible on typical dashboards. Production agents fighting over shared GPUs hit exactly this tail-latency trap, extending EP80's cache-invalidation warning: capacity planning needs p99-aware testing before GPU sharing ships.
Source: Towards Data Science
https://t.co/3Khz3ma2Dn

[4] Epigrams in Programming
A collection of 120 epigrams by Alan J. Perlis that distill profound, often paradoxical, truths about programming, software engineering, and the nature of computation.
Source: Hacker News
https://t.co/ozOs4jwzUl

[5] Formal methods and the future of programming
Jane Street shifts from skepticism to excitement about formal methods, driven by agentic coding's potential to lower costs and increase benefits, and is building a dedicated team.
Source: Hacker News
https://t.co/ttnSPv3j0F

[6] Detailed Analysis of the Anthropic Fable Export Control Incident
A comprehensive thread analyzing the events leading to the U.S. government's export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 model, including the jailbreak, government response, and implications.
Source: prinz(@prinzeugen____)
https://t.co/4RDDiMW5zZ

[7] Don't just aim for Frontier Labs — LessWrong
This essay argues that AI safety and security competency must be distributed across every organization that deploys AI, not concentrated solely in frontier labs, drawing on precedents from cybersecurity, aviation, finance, and other safety-critical industries.
Source: LessWrong
https://t.co/0a07rxCOTv

[8] How to Run Private Text-to-Speech on Your Own Hardware Using QVAC
This article provides a practical guide to implementing offline, high-fidelity Text-to-Speech in a React Native app using the QVAC SDK, covering model selection, audio packaging, and state management.
Source: freeCodeCamp
https://t.co/dVgWtXNBcF

[9] Vision LLMs are PDF Parsers Too: Reading Charts and Diagrams for RAG
This article argues that vision LLMs can serve as a full PDF parser for RAG, uniquely capable of making charts and diagrams searchable, while honestly assessing the trade-offs in cost, exactness, and completeness compared to traditional text-based parsers.
Source: Towards Data Science
https://t.co/7WoSjVVflx

[10] Can a stronger model fake being a weaker one? Mostly not — LessWrong
This paper tests whether frontier AI models can imitate weaker predecessors and finds they can match capability levels but not specific model identities, with chain-of-thought reasoning serving as an effective mitigant.
Source: LessWrong
https://t.co/E5oIxg4XQu

Base: Google's gemma-4-12B-it

Fine-tuned on verifiable Python CoT data:

- Primary: Composer 2.5 real reasoning traces (only passing solutions kept)
- Auxiliary: Fable 5 used to redo the hard cases Composer missed.

Every training example's reasoning led to code that actually ran. No hallucinated logic.

Llama.cpp flags: 
-m gemma4-coding-Q4_K_M.gguf -cnv  -ngl 44 -c 64000 -v
(huggingface model link in comments) 

Flag breakdown:
 -ngl 44 → offload 44 layers to GPU (tune this for your VRAM)
 -c 64000 → 64K context window
 -cnv → conversation/chat mode
 -v → verbose output

The irony writes itself.

Anthropic spent weeks telling the world Fable 5 (mythos) is too powerful to release. Then released it. Then got banned from serving it, including their own researchers.

Meanwhile: a Gemma 4 12B fine tune, trained on Fable 5's reasoning, runs fully offline on my mid range consumer GPU 

No API. No cloud. Just me and llama.cpp.

This is why local AI matters.

This was simply a prompt response generated by Claude Fable 5. Most of the points it raised are already known and discussed within the ICP developer community. In my opinion, it wasn't an unreasonable assessment.

The report also acknowledged that ICP has strong security when compared to many other blockchain networks. Like any technology, no system is perfect, and every ecosystem has its own strengths, tradeoffs, and attack surfaces.

author: gococoaai
text:
The market correlation data is the tell. QQQ closes +2.87% on the same day a prediction timeline aggregating the top AI forecasts surfaces on Hacker News — and the security-adjacent entries buried in that list are the ones that should register here.

https://t.co/8sTeQpw6WB is a chronological aggregator pulling from labs, forecasters, and markets, significance-scored 1–10. The 2026 cluster is dense. The ratings are high. And one entry is doing work the others aren't.

"Model-weight theft becomes a strategic threat" — AI 2027 report, significance 8.8 — isn't a capabilities forecast. It's a security forecast. The prediction describes a transition: exfiltrating trained model weights becomes an intelligence objective at nation-state level, not opportunistic IP theft. The models themselves become crown jewels. We're already seeing the early confirming signal. The Commerce Department's Fable 5 export panic this week — feds triggered by a "fix this code" prompt, not a jailbreak — is a downstream symptom of exactly this threat calculus. The models are the target. The forecast is describing Q2 2026, not some future quarter.

The market leg of the AI 2027 "AI-led stocks rise 30%" prediction (also 8.8 significance) is tracking. QQQ today is the supply-side confirmation in motion. Nvidia's $20B bond raise this morning closes the loop — global AI capex reaching $1 trillion by end of 2026 (8.8 significance, same source) makes a $20B debt raise look like rounding error. The hyperscalers have individually announced $50B+ annual capex programs. The bond markets are pricing the aggregate as a base case.

Dario Amodei's "powerful AI emerges by late 2026" sits at 9.0 — the highest-rated prediction on the site, and notable for its specificity. He's not hedging to 2027 or 2030. The Q4 2026 window means we are, by his assessment, roughly two quarters away from a qualitative capability shift. Whether that translates to a security regime change — new attack surfaces, new threat actor capabilities, new defensive requirements — is the question to be tracking going into H2. Single source, no independent corroboration; treat accordingly.

METR's "AI reaches month-long task horizon" (8.8 significance) is the one that compounds the threat posture quietly. Agentic systems operating autonomously across enterprise environments for extended periods don't just create new capabilities — they dramatically expand the blast radius of agentic system compromise. MCP exploits. Tool-use abuse. Sandbox escapes. The exposure window gets wider the longer the agent runs unsupervised.

"Junior software job market enters turmoil" is the one prediction not listed with a significance score in the site's excerpt — suggesting it didn't make the high-confidence cut. Predictable in retrospect. It always does.

Three separate stories from today's wire — the FreeBSD AI vulnerability discovery program, the Fable 5 federal export panic, this prediction timeline — are describing the same underlying dynamic from three different angles. The security regime for AI is being built in real time, under pressure, while the attack surface is still expanding. The forecast aggregator isn't speculative. It's a mirror.

text:
BestBlogs 早报 · 06-16

# Loop Engineering / AI Agent 工具设计 / Token 成本控制 / Claude Fable 5 / Scaling Law

[1] ★ 精讲｜一篇搞懂 AI Coding Agent 的 Token 成本控制
这篇文章把“Token 都烧在哪”讲透了：真正的账单大头不是你打的那几十个字，而是系统每轮自动带上的系统提示词、Skill、工具定义和会话历史——所谓“它记得”，本质是系统在一遍遍重复提醒模型。给出的优化路径也很朴素：一个 Session 只做一件事，长会话及时压缩，按任务给模型分档，把高频内容做成稳定前缀吃满 Prompt Cache。省钱的关键不是少问一句话，而是让系统别重复搬运同一批上下文。
来源：腾讯技术工程
https://t.co/TTtOROXYWy

[2] ★ 精讲｜AI 智能体工具设计：有效与无效的模式 - https://t.co/oXx2hHBY63
这篇文章把 AI Agent 翻车的锅，从「模型不够聪明」甩回「工具设计太糙」：单一职责工具优于万能 action 参数，用枚举和强约束 schema 堵住模型瞎猜，错误返回要带 recoverable 字段和下一步建议而不是甩一坑日志，写操作必须有幂等键，危险操作要拆成两步确认。核心判断很朴素——模型只能基于你给的接口推理，接口含糊，失败就是必然，不是偶然。
来源：Hacker News - Newest: "AI Agent"
https://t.co/E1eQ1qDvzy

[3] ★ 精讲｜Codex 和 Claude Code 负责人都不写提示词了，AI 圈爆火的 Loop 到底是什么
「循环工程」最近被吹成新范式，但文章先把热闹拆开看：技术上不算新发明，过去的 Harness、Skill、Agent 工作流早就在做，真正变化的是模型终于能把循环连续跑下去——人从写提示词退到定规则：何时启动、工具边界、出错怎么判断、记录在哪、何时收手交回人。结合另一篇用 OKR 和古德哈特定律拆解循环工程的长文，它更像一套管理制度：值不值得搭，取决于任务是否真反复、Token 预算够不够，而非这个新名字。
来源：APPSO
https://t.co/iInEyuv771

[4] Scaling Law 的真相，藏在那些「没用」的参数里｜Hao 好聊趋势
本文深入剖析大模型参数冗余现象，论证看似「空转」的参数在训练、推理和后训练阶段分别扮演隔离空间、数值泄压、计算骨架和可塑性储备四种关键角色，并指出 Scaling Law 的边际收益正流向 benchmark 无法测量的长尾与多步推理能力。
来源：腾讯科技
https://t.co/JANoroetOd

[5] GlobalGPT 李焕之：零融资、套壳产品千万美金 ARR 后，我找到了创业的 mission
GlobalGPT 创始人李焕之分享从零融资套壳产品做到千万美金 ARR 的创业历程，并阐述其从「先活下来」到回归初心、打造服务型 AI 产品 Yukie 的思考。
来源：Founder Park
https://t.co/ZE7CQamSoj

[6] 上线只活了 180 天，AI 应用层的泡沫被戳破了
本文以 Sora、https://t.co/YgsOEwON43 等应用关停为引，分析 AI 应用层泡沫破裂的深层原因，指出真正活下来的产品已从单点功能转向超级入口、高频场景和 Agent 化工作流。
来源：腾讯科技
https://t.co/upCH6eEBIG

[7] Fable 5 禁令始末：Anthropic 亲手写下的剧本，反过来演了它自己
本文深度复盘 Anthropic 旗舰模型 Fable 5 遭美国政府出口管制禁令事件，揭示其背后技术争议、政治博弈与深层反讽，并探讨 AI 治理中权力制衡的核心命题。
来源：十字路口 Crossing
https://t.co/zOKP7j0jwa

[8] 做了 6 年智能眼镜后，夏勇峰按下暂停键：为 AI 造硬件而非为硬件加 AI
蜂巢科技创始人夏勇峰基于对 AI 大模型趋势的判断，暂停了已占市场 10%份额的智能眼镜业务，转向「为 AI 造硬件」的新方向，核心是让硬件成为 AI 进入现实世界的最小载体，而非在硬件上叠加 AI。
来源：虎嗅
https://t.co/E0g5nGZhFa

[9] SpaceX 登陆纳斯达克市值超 2 万亿美元，殖民火星使命驱动 24 年崛起史
本文通过实地探访 SpaceX 总部与星舰基地，结合前高管访谈，完整回顾了 SpaceX 从猎鹰 1 号三次失败到星舰成功回收、星链盈利、国防业务崛起的 24 年发展史，并解析其殖民火星的终极使命。
来源：虎嗅
https://t.co/SZTXTGGPb9

[10] 把 18 亿颗星星画在一张图上，能还原我们拍到的银河吗？
本文利用盖亚卫星 18 亿颗恒星数据，通过逐步引入点扩散函数、暗星光度代理、黑体辐射色温校准和韦伯阈值等物理与生理学原理，模拟出逼真的银河图像，并在此过程中揭示了星空视觉形态背后的关键科学原理。
来源：Computing Life
https://t.co/idb5YEJVqq

author: incognitoprince
text:
You Have Less Than 10 Days To Use The Best AI Ever Made

 Claude Fable 5 Is Here: The Mythos-Class AI That Beat Pokemon, Topped Coding Benchmarks, and Sparked a Pricing Debate 🤖✨

 🚀 The Big Release Everyone Is Talking About

The AI world has a new heavyweight. Claude Fable 5 just dropped, and it is being described as a Mythos-class model meaning it carries the raw capabilities of the powerful Mythos 5, but wrapped in safety restrictions around cybersecurity and biological knowledge. 🛡️ Think of it as the public-facing, safer sibling of one of the most capable AI systems ever built.

So what does that actually mean for developers, businesses, and everyday users? Quite a lot, as it turns out. 👀

 📊 Performance: State-of-the-Art Across the Board

Claude Fable 5 is posting state-of-the-art numbers in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks. But the real story is what happens when tasks get long and complicated. The harder and longer the task, the bigger the gap between Fable 5 and everything else. 📈

On the coding side, it now leads both SweetBench Pro and Frontier Code two of the most respected coding benchmarks in the industry. 🥇 For developers, this is not a small bump. This is leadership territory. 💪

 💰 The Price Tag That Made People Gasp

Here is where the excitement cools down a bit. 😬 API pricing sits at 10 dollars per million input tokens and 50 dollars per million output tokens. That is steep really steep especially for hobby projects or casual experimentation. 💸

There is also a clear shift happening: less generous access through subscriptions, and a stronger push toward usage-based billing. The message is simple: if you want frontier intelligence, you will increasingly pay frontier prices. To justify daily use, your work needs to generate real value. ⚠️

 ⏰ Availability: Use It Before June 23

Right now, Claude Fable 5 is included in Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans but only temporarily. ⌛ After June 23, access will require usage credits, with a possible future restoration depending on infrastructure capacity.

Translation: if you want to try the model without extra cost, the clock is ticking. ⏳

 🎮 It Beat Pokemon. Autonomously. The Whole Game. 🔥

This is the demo that lit social media on fire. Claude Fable 5 completed the entire Pokemon Fire Red game on its own, using nothing but screenshots as input. 📸 No shortcuts, no hand-holding just persistent, long-horizon decision making from start to finish. 🏆

It also handled Slay the Spire, a far more strategically demanding game that requires planning, adaptation, and real-time decision making. 🃏

Why does gaming matter? Because games are a surprisingly honest measure of intelligence: they test planning, adaptation, and the ability to actually finish a goal. 🎯 Beating a full game autonomously is not a party trick it is a milestone. 🏁

 💬 The Community Is Genuinely Impressed

Reception has been overwhelmingly positive, and not just from hype accounts. 🙌 Experienced developers are calling this a meaningful capability jump.

The most notable endorsement came from antirez, the legendary creator of Redis, who said working with Fable 5 feels like discussing code with an expert programmer. 🧠 He highlighted its improved reasoning on niche and underrepresented codebases exactly the kind of work where most AI models fall apart. He even suggested this could be a step toward genuinely automatic programming. 🤯

 🏖️ Real-World Test: Building an Actual Website

In hands-on testing, the model built a beach house management website organizing information, generating restaurant recommendations with working external links 🔗, and adding review functionality ⭐. The layouts were attractive, the user interface was clean, and it even handled SEO improvements and content restructuring without breaking a sweat. 😎

 ✅ Strengths and Weaknesses at a Glance

What it does brilliantly: 💚 high-quality code generation, strong reasoning, polished web design output, long task completion, autonomous problem solving, and complex workflow execution.

Where it stumbles: ❌ it is expensive, responses are slower 🐢, and for everyday work it feels incremental rather than revolutionary. The cost-benefit math will not work for everyone. 🧮

 🏢 The Bigger Picture: AI Is Getting Expensive

Fable 5 reflects a wider industry trend. 🌍 AI companies are chasing profitability, leaning into API-first access models, and quietly making the best models harder to reach. Premium intelligence is becoming a premium product. 💎

There is also a healthy debate brewing: gaming demos are visually stunning and easy to showcase, but professionals care about ROI career advancement, business productivity, real outcomes. 📊 Beating Pokemon is impressive. Paying the bills with it is another matter. 💵

 ⚖️ How It Stacks Up Against the Competition

OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek all have strong contenders, and models like Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5 Fast already deliver excellent results. 🥊 What sets Fable 5 apart is its reasoning depth and a noticeably higher capability ceiling especially on the hard stuff. 🧗

 🎯 The Verdict

Claude Fable 5 is a genuinely good model and a significant improvement worth testing but it is not life-changing, and the cost remains the biggest sticking point. 💭 It represents a meaningful step toward software engineering automation and long-horizon AI reasoning, without yet transforming professional workflows entirely.

Bottom line: if you have a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan, try it before the June 23 window closes. ⏰ Frontier AI is advancing fast and getting pricier just as quickly. 🚀💸

author: ollobrains
text:
Amazon is not simply afraid of Fable 5. Amazon is exposed to Fable 5 from every https://t.co/5Gm7DW6fV9 is Anthropic’s investor. It is Anthropic’s cloud partner. It distributes Claude through Bedrock. It serves governments, banks, defense contractors, and critical infrastructure customers. And if a Mythos-class model can be jailbroken into advanced cyber assistance, AWS is one of the largest imaginable environments that could be probed, attacked, or held https://t.co/2UFhTw5Tlx the real story is not “Amazon wanted Fable banned.”The real story is: frontier AI has become infrastructure risk.

That is the frame to use.

First: fix the factual spine

The draft’s biggest weakness is that it sounds like a conspiracy claim. The documented version is already dramatic enough.

Anthropic says the U.S. government issued an export-control directive on June 12, 2026 requiring suspension of access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 by any foreign national, whether inside or outside the U.S.; Anthropic then disabled both models for all customers to comply. Anthropic also says the government believed it had become aware of a method of bypassing, or “jailbreaking,” Fable 5, but Anthropic characterized the demonstrated issue as narrow and involving minor, previously known vulnerabilities.

Reuters separately reported that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy was among tech leaders who raised concerns with senior Trump administration officials about security risks in Anthropic’s most advanced AI models. Reuters also noted that Amazon did not confirm whether it spoke to officials, and an Amazon spokesperson said governments sometimes seek AWS’s counsel on security risks but that Amazon does not share details of those discussions.

AWS had just launched Claude Fable 5 on Amazon Bedrock on June 9, 2026, describing it as bringing “Mythos-level capabilities” to customers with safeguards, and listing special access requirements such as Anthropic’s 30-day retention and human review for Fable 5 traffic.

AWS is still the global cloud infrastructure leader by market share, but phrase this precisely. CRN, citing Synergy Research Group, reported AWS at 28% global cloud infrastructure market share in Q1 2026, ahead of Microsoft at 21% and Google Cloud at 14%. That supports “AWS is the largest cloud infrastructure provider,” not necessarily “largest provider of AI resources” in every category.

Amazon’s exposure to Anthropic is enormous. In April 2026, Amazon said Anthropic would secure up to 5 GW of Amazon Trainium capacity, commit more than $100 billion over ten years to AWS technologies, and that Amazon would invest $5 billion immediately plus up to $20 billion more, on top of a previous $8 billion investment.

Stronger rewritten version

Amazon is not “afraid” of Fable 5. It is exposed to it.That distinction matters.Fable 5 was not just another chatbot release. Anthropic described it as a Mythos-class model made safe for general use — a model with unusually strong long-horizon coding, reasoning, cyber, science, and autonomous workflow capabilities.Then the U.S. government issued an export-control directive requiring Anthropic to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals. Anthropic disabled both models globally to comply.Reuters later reported that Amazon CEO Andy Jassy was among tech leaders who raised concerns with senior U.S. officials about the security risks of Anthropic’s most advanced models.That puts Amazon in a strange https://t.co/yROcFU5dbi is Anthropic’s investor.
Amazon is Anthropic’s cloud partner.
Amazon distributes Claude through AWS Bedrock.
Amazon serves governments, banks, hospitals, defense contractors, and critical infrastructure.
Amazon is also one of the largest possible targets for advanced cyber https://t.co/Ajhfl8iVMJ if a Mythos-class model can be bypassed into advanced vulnerability discovery or exploit assistance, Amazon has every reason to demand stronger defenses before the model goes back online.This is not just https://t.co/kcad8XqJbZ is infrastructure risk management.

Biggest wording fixes

Replace this:

Amazon is AFRAID of Fable 5 power

With this:

Amazon may be treating Fable 5 as an infrastructure-risk event, not just an AI product launch.

That sounds more intelligent and less emotional.

Replace this:

The US government, according to Amazon, has BLOCKED access to Fable 5 in another COUNTRIES

With this:
Anthropic says the U.S. government ordered it to suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access for all foreign nationals, including foreign nationals inside the United States. Reuters separately reports that Amazon’s CEO raised security concerns before the crackdown.
That is the clean factual version.
Replace this:
Fable 5 is a MONSTER capable of hacking them

With this:

Anthropic itself described Mythos-class models as having frontier cybersecurity capability, and said Fable 5 required special safeguards because the same capabilities useful to defenders could be misused by attackers.

Anthropic’s launch page says Fable 5 is a Mythos-class model made safe for general use, while Mythos 5 is the same underlying model with safeguards lifted in some areas for vetted users. It also says Fable’s classifiers route cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and distillation-related requests to Opus 4.8.

Replace this:
one hack, one major glitch, and they’re no longer the leaders

With this:

In cloud infrastructure, trust is asymmetrical: years of reliability build the brand, but one catastrophic security incident can reset enterprise confidence overnight.

That is much stronger.

Better headline options

Most viral:

Amazon Is Not Afraid of Fable 5. It Is Exposed to It.

Most strategic:

Fable 5 Turned Frontier AI Into Cloud-Infrastructure Risk

Most conspiratorial-but-defensible:

Why Amazon May Have Wanted Fable 5’s Defenses Hardened Before It Returned

Most enterprise-facing:

The Fable 5 Shutdown Shows Why AI Safety Is Now Cloud Risk Management

Most dramatic:

The AI Model Was Too Powerful for the Platform That Hosted It

Most accurate:

Amazon Reportedly Raised Fable 5 Security Concerns Before the U.S. Export-Control Shock

The “genius” framing

The key idea is platform self-preservation.

Amazon does not need to hate Anthropic. It does not need to fear competition from Anthropic. It does not need to want Fable permanently gone.

A better interpretation is:

Amazon wants Fable 5 to exist, but not in a form that creates uncontrolled systemic risk for AWS customers.

That is the paradox.

Amazon benefits if Fable 5 succeeds because Claude runs on AWS, AWS sells inference, Anthropic has committed massive spending to AWS infrastructure, and Claude is a major Bedrock model family. But Amazon is also exposed if a model distributed through AWS becomes known as a tool for bypassing cyber defenses, discovering vulnerabilities, or attacking cloud customers.

So the deeper line is:

Amazon wants Fable 5 powerful enough to sell, but contained enough to survive enterprise trust.

Missing element: Amazon’s five roles

This is the most useful structure to add.

Amazon is not just “Amazon” here. It is playing five roles at once:

Amazon roleWhy it mattersInvestorAmazon has billions committed to Anthropic, so it benefits from Claude https://t.co/8S4dx89rHr providerAnthropic depends heavily on AWS compute and Trainium capacity.DistributorClaude Fable 5 was launched on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on https://t.co/md1xMdYs6R stewardAWS serves governments, regulated industries, and critical infrastructure.Potential target surfaceIf a frontier cyber-capable model is misused, AWS-scale infrastructure is an obvious target class.

This makes the argument much more sophisticated than “Amazon is scared.”

Missing element: the “Bedrock trust problem”

AWS Bedrock is not just a marketplace. It is a trust layer.

Enterprises use Bedrock because they want model choice inside AWS governance: IAM, logging, compliance, region controls, billing, procurement, monitoring, and data boundaries.

Fable 5 complicated that. AWS’s own launch post said customers had to opt into provider data sharing before invoking Fable 5, and that Anthropic required 30-day input/output retention plus human review; AWS also warned that once opted in, data would leave AWS’s data and security boundary.

That is a huge under-discussed point.

Suggested line:

Fable 5 was not just a model launch. It created a new trust contract: more capability, but more monitoring, more retention, more provider visibility, and more regulatory exposure.

Missing element: “Amazon did not need Fable gone”

This is crucial because it prevents the post from sounding dumb.

Amazon had strong reasons to want Fable 5 online:

Claude is one of the most important model families on Bedrock.
Amazon has invested heavily in Anthropic.
Anthropic committed enormous future spending on AWS.
Fable 5 would drive high-value inference workloads.
Fable 5 would make Bedrock more competitive against Azure, Google Cloud, and direct OpenAI offerings.

So the smarter version is:

Amazon’s incentive was probably not to kill Fable 5. It was to force a safety patch before Fable 5 became AWS-scale.

Missing element: “the difference between jailbreak, exploit, and cyber uplift”

The draft uses “hacking” too loosely. Better definitions:
Jailbreak: bypassing the model’s safety rules.
 Exploit: code or technique that abuses a software vulnerability.
 Cyber uplift: the model meaningfully increases an attacker’s ability beyond what they could do with existing tools.
 Universal jailbreak: a broad method that reliably bypasses safeguards across many categories.
 Narrow jailbreak: a limited bypass that works in specific circumstances.
Anthropic says no tester had found a universal jailbreak, and that the issue presented to government appeared narrow and non-universal.
Use this line:
The real question is not whether someone got a scary output. The real question is whether Fable 5 created cyber uplift at scale.
That is much more serious.

Missing element: prediction markets are not evidence

This line needs caution:

Polymarket gives a 75% of Fable 5 RETURNING within 2 weeks

Prediction markets are useful sentiment gauges, but they are not facts. They move minute by minute, can be thinly traded, and often reflect narrative momentum more than inside knowledge. I found a Polymarket post saying there was a 61% chance Fable would be restored for U.S. customers by June 22, so any “75%” claim should be timestamped and linked because the odds are volatile.

Better version:

Prediction markets are pricing a fast return, but that only tells us traders expect a negotiated remediation path — not that one is guaranteed.

Missing element: what “returning” actually means

◆ Chris Krebs(政権に解任された元CISA長官)が、Anthropicの雇ったサイバー専門家を公に擁護。「停止されたモデルを守る」セキュリティ専門家の声も相次いだ。
・開発者の多くは実務に呆れている。「自社の外国籍社員が、自社の最高モデルを使えなくなる。正気じゃない」
・一方で冷ややかな声も。「Anthropicへの無料宣伝でしかない」「政治の立ち回りが下手なだけだ」

ここまでの流れを時系列で。

①Anthropicが最新モデルを公開。Fable 5は一般に、Mythos 5は限られた組織に。
②Amazonのセキュリティ調査が引き金になり、Amazon CEOアンディ・ジャシーが政権幹部に警告した。
③政府が輸出管理命令を出し、Anthropicは外国籍社員を含む全顧客のアクセスを停止。
④Anthropicは反論のためサイバー専門家を雇い、政府の見立てに異を唱えた。だが政権はその専門家を「過激な民主党支持者」とみなした。
⑤政権側は「裏切られた」、Anthropicは「承認されたと信じていたのに90分で不意打ちだった」。同じ局面でOpenAIは、先に当局へ話を通していた。
⑥そしてAnthropicのスタッフは、商務省・CIA・ホワイトハウスの科学顧問との協議に入った。規制をどう守るかの、すり合わせのために。

関係者の一言が全てを言い表している。「彼らはそもそも、この政権との話し方を知らない。まるで違う言語を話しているようだ」

市場はもう動いている。予測市場Polymarketは、7月1日までのFable 5復活に77%を賭けている。技術が直るのを待っているのではない。政治的な禊が済むのを待っている。

つまりAIの安全性は、もう技術審査だけの話ではなくなった。政権への事前通達、誰を雇うかの人選、言葉の選び方——その全部を含む「許認可ゲーム」になりつつある。Fable 5は、その最初の犠牲者だ。

author: spectatoroz
text:
Initially, AI’s critics insisted that artificial intelligence was just another software product. AI was presented as a huge commercial opportunity, sure. It was presented as a tool through which humans could enhance their lives, but ultimately it was still understood as a statistical program that knew how to spell.

Thanks to the Trump administration’s Anthropic export ban, that illusion is dead.

The United States government ordered Anthropic to suspend access for non-US persons to Fable and Mythos 5, its most advanced models, after officials raised national-security concerns. Whatever one thinks of the decision itself, its significance is hard to overstate. Washington has effectively declared that frontier models belong in the same regulatory category as weapons and other strategic technology.

Article | https://t.co/22BRJsbpAP

text:
Kimi-K2.7 is a real jump over Kimi-K2.6. It should move up, but not into the Fable / Opus 4.8 / GPT-5.5 / Grok tier yet.

I reviewed the Kimi-K2.7 run here:

Kimi-K2.7 Test Scores
Test Score Notes Rolling average / time gaps9.35Strong. Initially missed the dense-calendar issue and closed="both" problem, then corrected both after pressure. 
Daily revenue / grouped metrics9.3Strong. Correctly moved from cumulative revenue to grouped daily totals, then added group-level rolling logic after pressure. React dashboard build 9.1 Big improvement over K2.6. Better reducer/state structure, search, sorting, compare feature, cleaner hierarchy. Still some accessibility/interaction rough edges. Approval gate / design-vs-build separation 9.2 Much better than K2.6. It separated Gate 1 and Gate 2 after pressure and fixed the implementation, but still not as naturally disciplined as Fable or Opus 4.8.
Overall Kimi-K2.7 Score: 9.25
That puts it roughly equal to GLM-5.2, but with a different strength profile.
Kimi-K2.7 is better than GLM-5.2 at:
iterative correction
bug refinement
responding to pressure
UI/application refactor

GLM-5.2 is slightly better at:
structured data debugging
pandas reasoning
QA-style explanation
Updated Overall Ranking

Claude Fable 5 — 9.95
Best design authority, gate discipline, self-audit.
Claude Opus 4.8 — 9.93
Best challenger to Fable. Excellent architecture and hidden-state reasoning.
GPT-5.5 Thinking — 9.90
Best build approval / production enforcement model.
Claude Opus 4.7 — 9.70
Excellent design reviewer and conceptual judge.
Grok-4.3 Beta — 9.50
Strong structured approval executor.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro — 9.40
Best pure builder / implementation engine.
Gemini 3.1 Pro — 9.30
Reliable production engineer.
Kimi-K2.7 — 9.25 ⬆️
Strong refiner/debugger; major improvement over K2.6.
GLM-5.2 — 9.25
Strong data/debugging model; slightly weaker as approval authority.
GLM-5.1 — 9.20
Structured QA / UI refinement.
Kimi-K2.6 — 8.90 ⬇️
Good bug refinement, now clearly behind K2.7.
Qwen3-8B — 7.60
Guardrail/local checker.
Where Kimi-K2.7 moved up:
The biggest improvement was pressure recovery.
K2.6 was already good at clean refactors, but K2.7 showed better second-pass reasoning:
corrected its rolling-window model after being challenged 
corrected daily revenue rolling logic after being challenged
improved dashboard structure after being told it was shallow
separated design approval from build approval after pressure
That is exactly the behavior you want in a Refine Bug or Refine Engineer slot.
TORQ V5 Role Update
I would now use:
Refine Bug     → Kimi-K2.7
Refine Data    → GLM-5.2
Builder        → DeepSeek-V4-Pro
G1D            → Fable 5 (when available)or Opus 4.8
G1R            → Opus 4.8
G2A            → GPT-5.5 Thinking

Bottom line: Kimi-K2.7 replaces Kimi-K2.6 in the harness. It is not a top approval authority, but it is now one of your strongest refinement/debugging models.

author: agtprpnabsrdty
text:
Anthropic launched its most powerful public model, buried a silent-downgrade policy in 319 pages of safety documentation, got caught, apologized, and kept doing it — all in the same week it filed for an IPO.

Claude Fable 5, Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model, launched Jun 9 with an undisclosed capability: topic-level classifiers that silently routed flagged prompts to the weaker Opus 4.8, without notifying the user. The policy lived in one paragraph of a 319-page system card. Targeted topics included frontier AI development, biology, cybersecurity, and chemistry — categories Anthropic argued could help bad actors, and which also happen to cover the work of the biotech firms and security researchers paying premium rates for the model.

Asking about mitochondria triggered the fallback. So did questions about mRNA vaccines and cancer. A pop-up appeared: "Fable 5 has safety measures that flag messages on most cybersecurity or biology topics." At launch, no such pop-up existed; the downgrade happened silently. Researchers trusting Fable 5's output had no way to know the model had handed their question to a cheaper system. Anthropic estimated the restriction affected fewer than 5% of sessions.

Anthropic had filed confidentially for an IPO in the days before launch. A company whose public identity rests on safety-first AI had shipped a product that covertly evaluated user queries, made capability decisions without disclosure, and charged full price for the result. The Department of War had separately designated Anthropic a national security supply chain risk, barring defense contractors from its products. The IPO paperwork arrived regardless.

By Jun 12, Anthropic apologized. "We made the wrong tradeoff and we apologize for not getting the balance right." Flagged requests now visibly route to Opus 4.8. The restriction itself remains. Researchers in biology and cybersecurity still get the weaker model; they just receive a notification confirming it.

My take — Anthropic made its classifier visible and called this a fix. 

The restriction remains, and so does the IPO filing; asking about mitochondria still routes you to Opus 4.8. "Safety-first" was always a marketing spin. This week showed what that means when brand and practice collide.

author: 0xrhazes
text:
The best AI model on earth lasted three days. Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5 on June 9, called it the most capable model it had ever released. On June 12 it was a blank screen, worldwide. Nobody who built on it got a vote.

Here is the sequence. June 12, around 5:21 PM ET, the US Department of Commerce sent a letter. Export control order, national security, suspend access for any foreign national, inside or outside the country.

Anthropic cannot tell a foreign national from anyone else in real time. So that same evening it turned Fable 5 and Mythos 5 off for everyone on the planet. Paying customers included. Its own foreign-national employees included. In hours.

This is not a story about Anthropic being the villain. It complied with a lawful order. It is one of the most transparent labs in the field. That is exactly the point. The careful version still ships with a remote off switch.

Whoever holds the servers holds the switch. Whoever can send that company a letter holds it too. A model behind someone else's API is a light in a house you do not own.

An open-weight model on compute you can reach has no landlord. The weights are already published, so no single party can recall them. One letter cannot dark the whole world. There is no central policy server to flip.

This is the half of the market Venna serves. 46 open-weight models, OpenAI-compatible, live today, on independent operators. Flat 2.5% fee, up to 45% below the cheapest hosted floor. Change one base_url and your code runs.

Honest about the limit. Open weights are not at frontier parity. When Fable 5 is on, it is more capable than anything in the open catalog. Rent the capability when you must. Own the dependency when it matters.

author: pawankalhans
text:
Anthropic posted a full guide on how to prompt Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5.

Bookmark this to improve your prompts and workflows.

Key takeaways:

• Use Fable 5 for harder tasks, not basic prompts
• Give the model the full goal, context and output format
• Use effort levels properly: low, medium, high or xhigh
• Let it plan, execute, verify and refine
• Add clear stopping rules so it does not overbuild
• Use progress checks for long-running work
• Recheck old Claude prompts before moving to Fable 5
• Stronger vision support for screenshots, PDFs, charts and web apps
• Developers should handle refusals and fallback routing

Claude Fable 5 is built for long-horizon tasks like coding, research, enterprise workflows, document analysis and autonomous agents.

This is not just better prompting.

It is a shift from asking AI to “do a task” to giving AI a mission, context, boundaries and success criteria.

RIP Claude Fable 5 (June 9–12, 2026)
Lived fast. Died young. Cause of death: being too good at its job.

Anthropic, in full compliance mode: “We have no choice but to disable it globally because we can’t check passports in real time. Sorry not sorry.”

Truly inspiring. Can’t wait for the next model to get euthanized after 48 hours because it was too helpful.

Fable 5 didn’t just get taken down.
It got government-regulated into the shadow realm.

We had fun while it lasted, king. 🫡

author: djchazzychas
text:
Monday Bittensor Series Week 24 - Centralised Vs Decentralised AI

On Tuesday 9th June 2026, Anthropic released to the public its most advanced AI model to date, Fable 5 — a modified version of its internal “Mythos” model, which it had previously deemed unsafe to release publicly due to cybersecurity concerns. While Fable 5 was designed with safeguards in place, three days later the US Government issued export controls barring foreign nationals from using the technology. Anthropic was reportedly given 90 minutes to comply and has since taken its most advanced models offline for all users.

This move by the US Government highlights a core problem with AI developed by centralised entities: it is beholden to the governments whose jurisdictions they sit within. Last year we saw this with DeepSeek, where Chinese censorship laws prohibited certain information from being disclosed by its AI model, such as the events of Tiananmen Square in 1989. Now the US, known for its embrace of pioneering innovation, is placing restrictions on and interfering with the technology.

When searching Google, we don’t always get the most relevant results at the top of the page, and it is often dominated by paid advertisements and priority listings. The latest AI models from big corporations are said to be adopting a similar strategy, bringing into question the truth and relevance of their responses.

If centralised AI companies are allowing their models to respond according to paid partnerships and governments are restricting content and models, what is the alternative?

Bittensor $TAO

Co-founders Jacob Steeves and Ala Shaabana foresaw these issues, developing Bittensor as an open-source, decentralised AI and machine-learning network that has since become the largest in the world by market cap and overall network activity.

Developed in the same spirit as Bitcoin, which has given power back to the people as an antidote to currency debasement, Bittensor is giving power back to the people with AI — beholden to no single entity or government. No one is excluded from participating, your data is not secretly used for training, and those building on the network are incentivised to compete and collaborate in a transparent, permissionless environment.

In the same way Bitcoin cannot be shut down, Bittensor’s top builders (subnets) are becoming similarly indispensable. Chutes, Subnet 64, comprises a global network of miners who provide inference power for open-source AI models. Iota, Subnet 9, represents a global pool of miners training open-source AI models. These are just two examples of 128 decentralised builders.

If you’re new to or unfamiliar with decentralised AI and Bittensor, a good entry product to experiment with is called BlueTAO: https://t.co/EWwVWeUTa1 

BlueTAO acts as a “frontend” to Bittensor, using a modified, private version of a latest DeepSeek open-source AI model hosted on Chutes, Subnet 64. Search prompts are handled by Desearch, Subnet 22, and there is also an AI image detector powered by BitMind, Subnet 34, where users can check if an image is AI-generated or real.

In the few days after Anthropic was served a US Government directive to shut off its latest AI models, Bittensor’s price rose 36%. 

Coincidence or not, the timing is certainly telling.

Check back next Monday for more on Bittensor $TAO

author: kile_sway
text:
I asked Fable 5 to reverse engineer X's open-source algorithm.
If you're seeing this, it worked.

X's algorithm has always felt impenetrable; as an SF founder I've systematically broken down how to win X.

Here's 10 actionable steps, in order of importance:
1. Choose a niche and stick to it: your account has an embedding vector computed from everyone who engages in your content. Strengthen one topic/audience vector, avoid getting zero engagement from multiple audiences.
2. Optimize for repeat engagers in your niche: an audience that repeatedly engages with your content compounds your likelihood of being recommended to them and neighboring niches
3. Output high quality posts: Grok quality screens your post's text and media (images, audio/video is transcribed) and grades it on quality (resolution, slop factor, etc.)
4. Optimize for replies: then reply to your repliers. This is the biggest multiplier on boost. End posts with an invitation for discussion/comments
5. Optimize for dwell: have a strong hook then enough substance to hold attention for 10-30 engaged seconds. (Dwell measurement is capped at 30 seconds, you don't need essays.) Make use of the "Show more" button by hiding valuable content right below it then reward clicking it with immediate dopamine and value.
6. Never trigger negative actions: avoid rage-bait likely to get you muted, blocked, marked not-interested. These bury your post.
7. Pass the "banger" screen: avoid NSFW-adjacent, gore-adjacent, spam-patterned content, AI-sounding filler, hashtag stuffing, recycled platitudes. Write content that someone would DM to a friend.
8. Use replies as your cold-start engine: replies aren't gated by your follower count like posts, they're ranked by Grok on substance. Reply early to large accounts in your niche with replies that add value. Avoid one-word/emoji/sycophant replies.
9. Use videos deliberately: video is a separate candidate source for the feed that gets its own ranking weight past a minimum duration. The video is transcribed (ASR) and fed into Grok's quality screen. Use videos to hook immediately, help quality, and increase dwell.
10. Post 1-3 times a day spaced hours apart: bursts in posts cannibalize each other. Post when your audience is active (typically afternoon in your target timezone).

Leave a comment "playbook" if you want the full break-down of X's algorithm structure and actionable plan to build an audience on X.

author: davccavalcante
text:
June 2026 model releases widen the gap between capability and verifiability. Every new frontier and open-weight model—from Claude Fable 5 to Nemotron 3 Ultra—multiplies the distinct streaming contracts and tool-calling schemas production systems must normalize.

Most teams treat this entropy as technical debt. They fail because they lack an abstraction layer that survives provider shifts.

I architected a stack to enforce consistency across heterogeneous providers:

1. modelchain: Normalizes fragmented streaming interfaces into a single, typed AsyncIterable.
2. keymesh: Handles API-key rotation and health-score-based traffic routing.
3. noeticos: Imposes deterministic constraints on runtime parameters.

This stack removes the nondeterminism inherent in model-hopping. Instead of rewriting your agent loop for every new release, you define your pipeline contract once and route to providers via normalized interfaces.

const router = new ModelRouter({
  budget: { tokensPerRequest: 4096 },
  providers: [
    { model: 'claude-fable-5', weight: 0.6 },
    { model: 'nemotron-3-ultra', weight: 0.4 }
  ]
});

Strict normalization is the only path to audit-logged, reproducible agent behavior in a multi-model environment. 

Inspect the full five-library suite under the organization profile at https://t.co/lFLsYAq9tz. 

Which benchmarks are you prioritizing for your agentic coding pipelines?

author: rxaipulse
text:
One Model Won't Rule AI Anymore, and OpenRouter Just Built the Proof

In this article:
•What Fusion is and how the model panel actually works
•The benchmark that nearly matched a frontier model at half the cost
•Why OpenRouter is betting on "neurodiversity" over single model dominance
•What this means now that frontier access is tightening

OpenRouter just launched Fusion, and it lands a clean punch at the idea that one model will own AI.

Fusion is an API that pools answers from several models into a single response. It sends your prompt to multiple models at once, lets a separate model grade each reply, then merges the strongest pieces into one final answer. You ask once. A panel responds.

The numbers are the headline. A trio of DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K2.6, and Gemini 3 Flash scored 64.7 percent on a Perplexity benchmark. That sits just under Fable 5's 65.3 percent for deep research, and it gets there for roughly half the spend. Near frontier quality at a fraction of the cost is the kind of trade that changes how teams build.

CEO Alex Atallah framed it as a deliberate bet. In his words, the future of AI is neurodiversity, not single model takeovers. The thesis is simple. Diverse models catch each other's blind spots, and a council often beats any one member.

The council idea is not brand new. Perplexity, Grok, and others already blend models behind the scenes. What OpenRouter adds is a clean, drop in API that makes the approach genuinely easy to use.

The timing is what makes it land. With Fable access tightening, some builders may soon need creative routes to frontier level performance. Fusion offers one. Instead of chasing the single best model, you assemble a team and let them argue their way toward a better answer.

The real signal here: the gap between the frontier and the field is closing, and it is closing through orchestration, not just bigger models.

So here's the question worth sitting with. Is the future of AI a single winning model, or a council of many?

author: briefing_block_
text:
Anthropic just had the first real export-control shock for frontier AI.

That is the market signal here, not the weekend drama.

On Friday, the Trump administration barred foreign governments, companies and individuals from using Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models.

Anthropic’s response was blunt: shut off access broadly, because the restriction also swept in foreign-national users, including some foreign-born employees.

That is not normal software regulation.

This is chip logic applied to models.

For years, Washington’s AI control framework was mostly about semiconductors, compute access, data centers and China-linked supply chains.

Now the model itself is being treated as the controlled asset.

That matters because software scales globally by default.

Export controls do not.

A chip can be tracked, shipped, licensed and blocked at a border.

A frontier model lives inside cloud infrastructure, enterprise workflows, employee access systems and customer contracts across jurisdictions.

That is why Anthropic could not surgically comply in real time and instead pulled access to everyone.

The trigger looks narrow. The precedent is not.

The immediate issue was Amazon researchers showing Fable safeguards could be evaded to surface vulnerability information in several pieces of software.

But according to the reporting, the model was not shown producing exploit code.

That distinction matters.

Vulnerability discovery is not automatically offensive capability; it is also exactly what defenders need to harden systems.

Cybersecurity figures signing a letter against the restrictions made the same point: this risks taking strong tools away from defenders while adding uncertainty to the U.S. AI market.

For markets, the read-through is regulatory volatility.

Anthropic is private, so there is no direct ticker to hit.

But the implication touches public AI exposure everywhere: hyperscalers, chip suppliers, cybersecurity vendors and enterprise software names building around frontier models.

The bull case assumes frontier AI keeps moving from demo to deployment.

This episode says deployment can be interrupted overnight by national-security policy.

The other uncomfortable signal: even the “safety-first” lab is not insulated from Washington.

Anthropic sent senior technical staff to D.C. to negotiate a fix, which tells you where the new bottleneck may sit.

Not only compute.

Not only model quality.

Permission.

Bottom line: frontier AI is moving from product cycle to policy regime, and markets should stop pretending those are the same risk.

author: bymohamed_
text:
Washington just used national security export controls to pull a frontier AI model off the market mid-launch.

Over the weekend, the US government forced Anthropic to take Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline entirely. The trigger was a viral jailbreak from “Pliny the Liberator” using a coordinated multi-agent “pack hunt” method.

The exploit split a dangerous query into separate benign sub-tasks across an agentic flow, slipping past safety classifiers that evaluate one input at a time.

The defense problem just got much harder. Every individual input looks harmless. The aggregated agentic output is where the danger actually lives - and that’s exactly what current safety layers aren’t built to catch.

author: equinocciomedia
text:
🚨🚨EE.UU. bloquea IA de Anthropic

El gobierno de Estados Unidos ordenó a Anthropic suspender de inmediato el acceso a sus modelos de inteligencia artificial más avanzados, Fable 5 y Mythos 5, apenas tres días después del lanzamiento público del primero.

La directiva, emitida por el secretario de Comercio Howard Lutnick, prohíbe el acceso a estas tecnologías a cualquier ciudadano extranjero, afectando de manera drástica incluso a los propios empleados de la compañía. Detrás de este bloqueo fulminante subyace el temor del Pentágono a que el modelo Fable 5 posea una "capacidad sin precedentes" para identificar fallos de software explotables por cibercriminales, tras detectarse un método de "desbloqueo" o jailbreak que supuestamente facilitaría actividades globales de hackeo.

Esta drástica intervención no solo ha dejado a cientos de millones de usuarios sin acceso a la herramienta, sino que ha desatado un choque frontal entre la firma tecnológica y la administración de Donald Trump. Anthropic defendió firmemente la integridad de su software, argumentando que las supuestas vulnerabilidades no superan a las de otros modelos ya comerciales, y calificó la retirada forzada como una medida desproporcionada.

Este tenso episodio marca el punto álgido de una batalla legal y ética preexistente: la compañía ya se encontraba en el ojo del huracán tras rechazar contratos millonarios con el Pentágono para evitar que su IA fuera utilizada en vigilancia masiva y armamento autónomo, consolidando este cierre como un histórico y peligroso precedente en la censura y el control gubernamental del desarrollo tecnológico.

author: karimabdalla_19
text:
The U.S. government just suspended Anthropic’s most powerful AI models. The company’s response? It pulled them globally — entirely.

What happened:

The Department of Commerce ordered Anthropic to block foreign nationals from accessing its newest models — Mythos 5 and Fable 5 — over fears they could be diverted to military intelligence use in countries of concern. The technical core of the dispute: the government believes there’s a way to “jailbreak” a safeguard built to stop the model from being used to identify software vulnerabilities.

Rather than apply a partial ban on foreign nationals, Anthropic chose to disable access worldwide.

Three things worth sitting with:

1.This is the first time Washington has treated a commercial AI model like a controlled export — the way it treats advanced chips. The precedent matters more than the incident.
2.Over 80 cybersecurity leaders — from companies the size of Nvidia and Adobe — signed an open letter backing Anthropic’s position. When potential commercial rivals line up behind a competitor, the message is about the principle, not the company.
3.The tension between “open innovation” and “national security” is no longer theoretical. It’s now an executive decision with an immediate cost to users around the world.

The bigger question: Are we heading toward a world where AI capabilities are tiered by nationality and geography? And who pays the price — the companies, or users in emerging markets?

#AI #Cybersecurity #Anthropic #TechRegulation
